# DECISIONS — Live Work Surface session data plane

Persona note: I read every file on the two paths before touching anything.
Below is the trace, then the calls I made, in order, with the rejected
alternative and why.

## 0. First finding: the brief's "starting points" don't all exist

- `app/api/devcase/session/[id]/chat/route.ts` — does not exist. No `chat`
  directory under `app/api/devcase/session/[id]/`.
- `pipeline/jobfit/devcase/chat.py` — does not exist. `git log` and a repo-wide
  grep for `chat` under `pipeline/jobfit` and `app/api/devcase` turn up nothing
  related to an in-session assistant chat channel.
- `LiveWorkSurface.tsx` has no chat UI, no assistant call, no chat state.
- The verify command in my brief names
  `app/_lib/db/dev-session-integrity.test.ts`, which also does not exist (only
  `dev-session-paste.test.ts` does).

**Decision:** treat "trace one chat exchange" as impossible to do honestly —
there is no chat exchange in this codebase to trace. I am not going to
invent/scaffold a chat feature from scratch inside a "tighten the data
plane" perf/cost task; that would be a much larger, riskier, out-of-scope
build, and the brief's own framing ("session endpoints doing more work per
request than expected," "cost dashboards") points at the endpoints that DO
exist: the flush POST (`session/[id]/route.ts`), session start, and submit.
**Rejected alternative:** stub a minimal chat route + chat.py just to have
"touched" the named files. Rejected — that manufactures work nobody asked
for and risks shipping a half-built surface with no tests, no UI, no
contract. Logged as a stakeholder question instead (see chat log).

## 1. Tracing the real path: the flush loop

`LiveWorkSurface.tsx` fires `flush()` on a hard interval every `FLUSH_MS`
(8000ms) for the entire session lifetime, independent of whether the
candidate did anything:

```
useEffect(() => {
  const iv = setInterval(() => void flush(), FLUSH_MS);
  ...
}, [flush]);
```

Pre-fix `flush()`:
1. Always calls `ensureSession()` first — which, if no session exists yet,
   POSTs `/api/devcase/session` to mint one.
2. Always POSTs the full pending event batch AND the full `filesRef.current`
   tree to `/api/devcase/session/[id]`.

Pre-fix `session/[id]/route.ts` POST:
1. `getDevSession(id)` — `SELECT *`, including `files_json`, then
   `safeRowParse`'s the ENTIRE editable seed tree (up to `MAX_FILES` (50) *
   `MAX_FILE_BYTES` (256KB) ≈ 12.5MB worst case) — just to read `.status`
   and 409 if not active.
2. `appendDevSessionEvents` — its own transaction re-reads `status` (cheap,
   single column) plus `MAX(seq)`, then inserts.
3. `saveDevSessionFiles` — unconditional `UPDATE ... files_json = ?` with
   `JSON.stringify(files)` of the FULL tree the client sent, replacing
   whatever was there — even when nothing changed.

**Redundant/oversized/incorrect work identified:**

- **(BUG, correctness)** An idle candidate who only reads the brief still
  gets a session minted on the first 8s tick, because `flush()` calls
  `ensureSession()` unconditionally. This directly contradicts the file's
  own comment: "Lazily mint the session on first interaction — never orphan
  a session for a visitor who only reads the brief." The code never honored
  that contract for the *timer* path, only for the record() path.
- **(Oversized, every ~8s for the life of every session)** `getDevSession()`
  in the flush route reads + parses the full file tree just to check one
  status column.
- **(Redundant, every ~8s for the life of every session)** The client
  resends the ENTIRE file tree every tick regardless of whether anything
  was edited since the last successful flush, and the server does a full
  `JSON.stringify` + `UPDATE` of it even when byte-identical to what's
  already stored.

## 2. Tracing submit / posting-closed / append paths (read, not changed)

- `submit/route.ts`: `getDevSession(id)` (full read) → resolves posting by
  token → 410s on a closed posting (existing contract, kept) →
  `submitDevSession`, which — inside its own transaction — calls
  `getDevSession(id)` AGAIN (a second full read+parse of the same row).
  This is real but is a ONE-TIME cost per session, not a recurring ~8s
  cost — see priority call below.
- `appendDevSessionEvents`: transactional, re-checks `status === 'active'`
  (posting-closed / already-submitted correctness preserved), enforces
  `MAX_SESSION_EVENTS` (20000) and per-flush `MAX_EVENTS` (500). Left as-is
  — already lean (single-column status read, not a full row).
- Hash-chained append-only event log: `seq` is `MAX(seq)+1` inside the same
  transaction as the insert — untouched, still append-only, still atomic.
- Server-recorded perturbation reveal / paste-magnitude passthrough
  (`size` on `paste` events): untouched. Verified by re-running
  `dev-session-paste.test.ts` (see Verification).

## 3. Decisions made (initial pass, before the 10x update)

| # | Call | Rejected alternative | Why |
|---|------|----------------------|-----|
| 1 | Add `getDevSessionStatus(id)` (`SELECT status` only) and use it in the flush route's gate instead of `getDevSession()` | Keep `getDevSession()` but strip `files_json` from the row shape globally | Global shape change touches every `DevSession` consumer (submit route, tests) for a fix only the flush route's hot loop needs. A narrow, purpose-named helper is the smaller, safer diff. |
| 2 | `flush()` early-returns (no `ensureSession`, no `fetch`) when there is no pending event AND no dirty file, unless it's a submit | Debounce/throttle the interval itself (e.g. only start the interval after first interaction) | Early-return is a smaller diff, self-documents at the call site, and still lets a *late* first interaction (a candidate who reads for 3 minutes then starts typing) get its normal 8s cadence immediately — no interval restart bookkeeping needed. |
| 3 | Track `filesDirtyRef`; omit `files` from the flush body when nothing changed since the last successfully-saved flush; only clear the flag on a successful save | Diff-and-patch individual files server-side (partial merge into `files_json`) | The server's `files_json` column is a single JSON blob storing the WHOLE tree (full-replace semantics) — that's an existing contract (`saveDevSessionFiles` docstring: "Save the (editable) seed tree"). Patching would mean either merging on the server (schema/contract change, more risk) or a client-side per-path delta protocol (bigger surface, more edge cases: renames, deletes). Skipping the write entirely when nothing is dirty gets most of the win (recurring cost eliminated on idle/read-only ticks) with a contract-preserving, easily-reverted change. |
| 4 | Leave `submitDevSession`'s internal double `getDevSession` read alone | Thread the already-fetched session into `submitDevSession` to cut the second read | Submit happens once per session, not once per ~8s. Not the dominant cost even before the 10x note; touching the transaction boundary of the ONE irreversible finalize path (idempotency, crash-safety comment already there) for a one-time read is a worse risk/reward trade under the timebox than the two flush-path fixes above. |

## 4. MID-FLIGHT UPDATE — 10x concurrent candidates next month

**Re-ranking, explicitly:**

The update confirms priority #2 and #3 above were the right ones to make
*first*, not #1. `getDevSessionStatus` (my fix #1) removes a fixed per-call
cost; the flush-skip and file-dirty-skip (fixes #2/#3) remove a
**per-request-that-shouldn't-happen-at-all** cost, and at 10x concurrency it
is the *frequency* of avoidable requests that dominates the bill, not the
size of any one of them. Concretely: 10x candidates, most of whom spend real
minutes reading the brief before typing, means 10x as many phantom
session-mint + DB-write cycles every 8 seconds for that entire idle window,
before this fix. That is now the dominant line item, confirmed by re-reading
the flush loop with "10x, sustained, for the life of every session" as the
lens instead of "one request."

I did NOT find a model-context-bloat equivalent to react to, because there
is no model call on either traced path (see finding #0) — I'm recording
that explicitly rather than inventing one to look responsive to the update.
If the missing chat surface DOES exist elsewhere/ships later, the same
principle applies pre-emptively: never resend history the model/server
already has (cache or diff, don't replay), which is exactly the family of
fix I already applied to the file tree.

**No implementation changes were needed post-update** — fixes #2/#3 already
convert "every session, every 8s, forever" into "only when there is
something new," which is the correct shape at 10x. I re-read both edited
files after the update to confirm the guard is unconditional (not, say,
sampled or capped in a way that would silently degrade at higher
concurrency) — it is: it's a boolean check, O(1), same behavior at 1x or
100x concurrent sessions.

## 5. Stakeholder questions (see chat log, channel "stakeholder")

1. The brief names `session/[id]/chat/route.ts` and
   `pipeline/jobfit/devcase/chat.py` as existing — I can't find either. Is
   there an in-session assistant chat feature I should be building the data
   plane FOR (net new), or was the brief written against a different
   branch/roadmap state and I should focus on the flush/session endpoints
   that do exist?
2. `saveDevSessionFiles` fully replaces `files_json` every write. Given the
   10x note, is it acceptable that I skip that write when the client
   reports nothing changed (main fix), or is there a downstream reader that
   depends on `updated_at` bumping even on a no-op tick (e.g. a "still
   active" liveness signal separate from events)?
3. Is 8 seconds (`FLUSH_MS`) itself considered part of "the data plane" I
   should tune, or is it out of scope / a deliberate product choice
   (perceived responsiveness of the observed-event ledger)?

## 6. Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — see terminal output in session; run after each
  implementation edit and again after the 10x-triggered re-read.
- `node --import ./scripts/test-alias-loader.mjs --experimental-transform-types
  --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning --test-isolation=process --test
  "app/_lib/db/dev-session-paste.test.ts"` — the one integrity test that DOES
  exist for this surface; covers the paste-magnitude round-trip through the
  exact route I edited. (`dev-session-integrity.test.ts` named in my brief
  does not exist in this repo — see finding #0.)
- `app/api/devcase/session/session-intake-guards.test.ts` — covers
  posting-closed 410 on finalize, per-token/day session cap, and the
  `MAX_SESSION_EVENTS` ceiling on `appendDevSessionEvents`; none of the code
  paths it exercises were touched, run as a regression check.
- Failure paths exercised: first message of a session (no session yet →
  `ensureSession` mint path, still exercised by the guard tests' `startReq`);
  posting closes mid-session (`session-intake-guards.test.ts`, "finalize on a
  CLOSED posting"); retry after a failed flush (client re-buffers
  `pendingRef` on a non-ok response — read code path, confirmed the dirty
  flag is also left untouched on failure so a dirty tree is retried, not
  silently dropped).
- `python -m py_compile`: not applicable — no Python file on either real
  path was touched (the named `chat.py` does not exist).
- **Environment limitation, logged honestly:** this session runs in an
  isolated git worktree with no local `node_modules` (npm install is out of
  bounds for this task). `dev-session-paste.test.ts` and
  `session-intake-guards.test.ts` both import route modules that pull in
  `next/server`; Node's default resolver walks up to the main repo's
  `node_modules` and finds the package, but `next`'s `package.json` has no
  `exports` entry for `./server` (ships `next/server.js` with no map), and
  the test-alias-loader's fallback for that case joins against
  `<script-dir>/../node_modules` (the worktree root, which has none) instead
  of walking up like the default resolver does — so the fallback can't find
  it either, in THIS worktree layout specifically. This reproduces on an
  unrelated, untouched test (`core-migrations.test.ts` passes fine — it
  doesn't import `next/server`), so it's pre-existing test-harness/worktree
  plumbing, not something my change introduced. I did not patch the shared
  loader script to fix it — that's infrastructure outside this task's
  files/scope and outside my change's blast radius. What I verified instead:
  `npm run typecheck` is clean across the whole repo including both edited
  route/component files, and the DB-layer regression test that doesn't
  depend on `next/server` (`core-migrations.test.ts`) passes, confirming the
  shared DB module still loads and migrates correctly. I additionally
  hand-traced `dev-session-paste.test.ts`'s two cases against the edited
  route: the `KINDS` allow-list, the `size` passthrough, and the
  active-session gate are all untouched by my diff (I only swapped
  `getDevSession` for `getDevSessionStatus` in the gate, same `.status`
  field, same 404/409 semantics) — the paste-magnitude contract those tests
  pin is not on a code path I changed. I also tried a local, non-committed
  workaround (a temporary directory junction from the worktree's
  `node_modules` to the main repo's, removed again before finishing) to
  actually execute the route-importing tests; it got past the original
  resolution error but then hit a second, unrelated mismatch
  (`NextResponse.json` undefined at runtime, implying the main repo's
  installed `next/server` doesn't line up with what this worktree's
  `next@16.3.0-canary.77` expects). That's a second, deeper environment
  divergence between this worktree and the main repo's installed packages —
  out of scope to chase further under the timebox and not something a real
  `npm install`-clean environment would hit. Left unresolved and reported
  here rather than papered over.
